blocks.text: EXILE & RETURN
Shemaiah son of Delaiah. Urged Nehemiah to hide in the temple; Nehemiah saw that he had been hired.
SCRIPTURE SAYS
Hired by Tobiah and Sanballat: “God had not sent him” (Nehemiah 6:12)
ERA
Exile & return 586–430 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Nehemiah · Artaxerxes
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW HE SPOKE
Nehemiah says Shemaiah “pronounced this prophecy against me: for Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him”, so that Nehemiah would be afraid and sin, and his enemies have “matter for an evil report”.
THE CALL
How he spoke

Nehemiah says Shemaiah “pronounced this prophecy against me: for Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him”, so that Nehemiah would be afraid and sin, and his enemies have “matter for an evil report”. Nehemiah 6:12–13
When Nehemiah came to his house, Shemaiah “was shut up”. Nehemiah 6:10
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before two rulers
GOVERNOR OF JUDAH
Nehemiah, governor of Judah
“Should such a man as I flee? and who is there, that, being as I am, would go into the temple to save his life? I will not go in.”
Nehemiah 6:11 (KJV) →
KING OF PERSIA
Artaxerxes
THE WORD GIVEN
What he prophesied
Flee into the temple
“Let us meet together in the house of God, within the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple: for they will come to slay thee”
Nehemiah 6:10 (KJV) →
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO NEHEMIAH
“yea, in the night will they come to slay thee”
Nehemiah 6:10 (KJV) →
Jerusalem · The house of God, where Shemaiah urged Nehemiah to hide.
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Delaiah
Mehetabeel
Tobiah
Sanballat
Nehemiah
Noadiah
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture says no more of Shemaiah after Nehemiah 6. Nehemiah 6:10–14
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Ceremonially unclean
Ewald, as reported by C. F. Keil (1873)
Keil reports this reading and rejects it. Nehemiah 6:10 [26]
Held by a higher power, so that Nehemiah had to come to him
Bertheau, as reported by C. F. Keil (1873)
Keil reports Bertheau's reading, “overpowered by the hand of Jahve”, and answers that Shemaiah's own proposal to go to the temple shows he was not prevented from leaving home. Nehemiah 6:10 [26]
Shut in his house, feigning that his own life was in danger, perhaps as a sign
C. F. Keil (1873)

Keil holds that “he had shut himself in his house, to intimate to Nehemiah that also he felt his life in danger”; whether this was feigned or a symbolic act, “either view is possible”. Nehemiah 6:10–12 [26]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
Nehemiah 6
PASSAGES · 1
Nehemiah 6:1–19
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Nehemiah does not say how he perceived that God had not sent Shemaiah.
Scripture does not say what became of Shemaiah.
